headline: Change is not a feature of the universe—it is the universe
universal_truth: Nothing permanent exists; flow is the fundamental nature of reality
fun_facts: Every atom in your body is replaced over about 7 years—you're literally not the same person
The Greek philosopher Heraclitus said 'you cannot step into the same river twice'—2,500 years ago
Even 'permanent' structures like mountains are slowly changing, just on timescales we can't perceive
discussion_questions: What change are you resisting that might be inevitable?
How has a painful change eventually led to something good?
If everything changes, what does that mean for how you live today?

hook.script: Look at your hand. Every atom in it will be replaced over the next several years. The cells in your stomach lining? Replaced in days. You are not a thing—you are a process, constantly renewing. Change is not what happens to you. Change is what you are.

cliff.script: We crave stability, permanence, something solid to hold onto. But physics, biology, and philosophy all tell the same story: nothing lasts. So why do we suffer so much over change? And how can we make peace with impermanence?
cliff.prompt: How can we accept that everything changes?

options.text: By releasing attachment to how things 'should' stay
options.response: Yes. Suffering comes from clinging to what is inherently temporary.

options.text: By focusing on what remains relatively stable
options.response: Finding stability helps, but even stable things eventually change...

fact1.title: You Are New
fact1.script: Your body replaces billions of cells daily. Your skeleton is completely renewed every 10 years. Your taste buds last about 2 weeks. The 'you' from 7 years ago shares almost no physical matter with the you today. You are continuity without permanence.

fact2.title: Heraclitus Was Right
fact2.script: 2,500 years ago, Heraclitus said: 'You cannot step into the same river twice—for it is not the same river, and you are not the same person.' Ancient wisdom that modern physics confirms. Reality is flux masquerading as substance.

fact3.title: Mountain Time
fact3.script: Mountains seem eternal, but they're eroding constantly—just slowly. The Himalayas rise about 5 millimeters per year. Even continents drift. There is nothing permanent in the universe—only different timescales of change.

wisdom.script: Here's today's wisdom: Fighting change is fighting reality. The art of living is learning to flow with impermanence—to hold things lightly, love fully, and release gracefully. Everything you love will change. Love it anyway.

outro.script: That's Day 30—one month of learning together. What a journey so far! Tomorrow, we'll discover how the sun powers all life on Earth. Until then, embrace change—it's the only constant.

growTrack.title: Impermanence Practice - Letting Go
growTrack.learning_objective: Practice acceptance of change through reflection
growTrack.activity: Think of something you're holding onto that's already changing or gone—a relationship, a phase of life, an old version of yourself. Write a short letter saying goodbye to it. Thank it for what it gave you. Then, symbolically release it.
